title: The Old Blue Castle Investigation Case
notes: Two-part episode, full transcript read for both parts. Recurring core cast (Conan Edogawa/Shinichi Kudo, Inspector Megure) omitted by the usual convention. Deviating from that convention for Agasa and the Detective Boys (Haibara, Ayumi, Mitsuhiko, Genta): they are included as person nodes here because this episode makes them direct present-day victims/investigators (kidnapped, attacked, and the ones who solve the case alongside the excluded Conan) rather than incidental bystanders, so omitting them would erase most of the present-day half of the graph. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved, sharing an `order` integer per real-world occurrence. The old flattened wiki-derived file at cases/ep136-137_... got the broad strokes right (maid Mutsumi Nishikawa killed and impersonated the real Masuyo Mamiya, motivated by a hidden treasure) but wrongly implied she killed the family's eldest daughter and 'several long-time servants' gradually 'over the following years' -- the transcript shows the daughter and roughly 10-15 guests/staff all died together in a single arson (the tower fire, 4 years before present) staged immediately after Masuyo's murder, on the same day, to cover it up; a second death (a suspicious employee, 2 years before present) is only implied, not confirmed on-screen. The old file also omitted Sada'aki Mamiya (the historian ex-owner whose will and cipher drive the whole B-plot), Mitsuru and Takahito's real family relationships, the chess-cipher/treasure-room mechanics, and the fact the 'treasure' turns out to be nothing. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Testimonial inconsistency: 'Masuyo' casually complained about passport photo sizes changing six years ago and about bill designs changing -- details someone truly housebound in the castle for the past decade (per her own claimed broken legs) could not have experienced firsthand -- proving she had secretly been coming and going, i.e. she is not the real, housebound Masuyo.

Forensic comparison: the recovered skeleton's leg bones are unusually thin and its teeth worn in a way consistent with someone who hadn't walked in roughly a decade, with a build and hairstyle matching an elderly woman -- inconsistent with the physically mobile, publicly active 'Masuyo' seen day to day, proving the skeleton is the real Masuyo and the woman posing as her is an impostor.
